name: Koropokkuru
body:
Koropokkuru are a species of reclusive humanoids who live in barren wilderness areas and seldom come into contact with humans. Many believe them to be distant cousins of dwarves and duergar.

Physical

Koropokkuru stand about 4 feet tall—at the lower boundary of the Medium size range.

They are lean but wiry, possessing a strength and athleticism that often surprises those who are not familiar with them. Their head is larger, and their arms and legs slightly longer, in proportion to their bodies than those of a human, and they walk with a slow but steady gait.

Koropokkuru have big, bright eyes that come in all the colors of the rainbow. Their ears are somewhat long, sometimes ending in a slight point. They have long thick hair that is usually black or brown, but can also come in many other colors—and usually turns gray or white with age. Male koropokkuru tend to bald as they age, and often grow long mustaches and beards.

Both men and women are fond of hats and bandanas woven of leaves and natural plant fibers, and flowers will often be worn in the hair for special occasions.

Koropokkuru favor simple, functional clothing, and craft such items out of natural items found in the wild. They prefer natural fibers such as cotton, and incorporate flowers, leaves, bamboo, and wood into their attire. They dress primarily in earth tones, camouflaging themselves into the surrounding terrain.

Social

The koropokkuru are mysterious and often misunderstood, as only live in the most remote areas of wilderness and rarely reveal themselves to humans. When they do encounter other humanoids, they can sometimes come across as belligerent, rude, and somewhat xenophobic, but they are rarely violent unless met with violence. An explorer with patience can eventually establish good report. Those who do form such an alliance will find not just a simple trading partner, but a strong, generous, and lasting friendship.

Koropokkuru culture revolves around the village, which is well-hidden in the remote wilderness. All members of the village contribute to its success, and to its existence in harmony with the wilderness. Men and women work together to hunt, fish, raise simple crops, gather what else they need, make tools and handcrafts, and enjoy each other’s company. For those that get to know the koropokkuru, they will find that they are a joyful people who love to eat, drink, sing, dance, tell jokes, and recount fanciful stories.

Koropokkuru also love magic and treasure, which they search for among the wild ruins or for with the fey and magical creatures no human has ever seen. This treasure is always jealously hidden away; koropokkuru will go out of their way to hide their wealth and magical ability.

Most koropokkuru have no interest in the “conveniences” of urban living and human society, and so they remain a hidden people. They are happy to interact with the fey and with outcast magical creatures of all kinds, but they are very wary of most standard humanoid species. Occasionally, an individual koropokkuru will be driven by curiosity or wanderlust to adventure to human lands. However, this curiosity usually does not last for long, and they almost always return to their village after they have seen the world—usually with some treasure to hide.

Alignment and Religion

Most of the koropokkuru are kind-hearted souls who work diligently to further the common good of everyone in their village.

There have even been tales of koropokkuru who have brought food and supplies to human villages in times of great need—although they are always very careful not to be seen.

While most koropokkuru lean toward Good, they have no preference for Law or Chaos. It is true that they are distrustful of strangers, but they are also very loyal to friends, and thus most opt for a balanced approach between collectivism and individualism in their lives.

Traditional koropokkuru religion is animistic, venerating the various nature spirits that reside near their village. Each village is led in these observations by one or more elders with levels in shaman, druid, oracle, or witch.

Base Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are resilient and intuitive, but lack any formal education. Your ability score adjustments are +2 Con, +2 Wis, –2 Int [standard].
Size As a Medium creature, you have no bonuses or penalties due to size.
Type You are a Humanoid with the dwarf subtype.
Speed Your base speed is 20 feet. Your speed is never reduced by armor or encumbrance.
Languages You begin play speaking Common and Koropokkuru. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Dwarven, Giant, Goblin, Sylvan, and Tengu.
Alternate Traits
Defensive Training Many koropokkuru undergo special training during which they learn tricks that previous generations developed in their battles with giants—especially ogres and oni. You gain a +4 dodge bonus to AC against creatures of the giant subtype.
Hardy You gain a +2 species bonus on saving throws against poison, spells, and spell-like abilities.
Hatred You gain a +1 species bonus on attack rolls against humanoids with the goblinoid and oni subtypes because of your special training against these hated foes.
Low-Light Vision You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions.
Lucky Once per day, when you roll a 1 on an ability check, attack roll, saving throw, or skill check, you can reroll. You must use the result of the new roll.
Skilled You are adept at getting along in the wilderness and staying hidden from prying eyes. You gain a +2 species bonus on Stealth and Survival skill checks.
